flagship.t_max.spec: the flagship champion's LARGEST realised |t| over all rivals. Reported beside t_binding because the gap between them is the whole point of the §2.2 correction

prop.hac_over_ceiling.spec: panels where the HAC-corrected |t| exceeds the i.i.d. ceiling. Proposition 2.2 is NOT stated for the HAC statistic and this does not extend it -- zero here is empirical reassurance on the panels at hand, not a proof, and S2.2 keeps the hedge

prop.median_slack.spec: median of |t| / ceiling on the binding pair -- the fraction of the bound the realised statistic CONSUMES, so a HIGHER value means LESS room, not more. Named `median_slack` for continuity with the acceptance ledger; the manuscript reports it as a ratio and does not call it slack, since that word inverts the reading. The bound is sharp in the sense that an extremal configuration attains it; this says how far the actual panels sit from that configuration, which is a different and more useful fact for a reader

prop.panels_sig_small_kstar.spec: panels with k* <= 3 AND a champion significant at the two-sided five-percent level against at least one rival -- a configuration §2.2 rules out only if the minimum-over-rivals bound is misread as binding every pair

prop.realised_violations.spec: panels where the realised i.i.d.-studentized |t| against the BINDING rival exceeds Proposition 2.2's ceiling for that pair. The proposition is stated per pair, so the binding rival -- the one that sets k* -- is the pair it constrains
